summary: Noxubee County, MS 100 ft MC-39 Aermotor on a former MFC county work center site; now privately owned; NHLR-registered July 2022 as US 1630; no build date or fire history found.

facts.design: MC-39 Aermotor tower, 100 ft; site was a county work center for the MFC
facts.status_note: Register describes the tower as 100 ft tall and standing, but gives no visit date or condition

access.note: Register says the site is now privately owned; no public access described in sources read

facts.agency: Privately owned; former Mississippi Forestry Commission county work center (MFC cooperator)

events.note: Registered July 4, 2022 as US 1630, MS 18; nominated by Jason Johns

evidence.supports: site was a county work center for the MFC and is now privately owned
evidence.quote: This site was a county work center for the MFC, but it is now privately owned.
The MC-39 Aermotor tower stands at 100ft tall.

evidence.supports: OpenStreetMap maps the tower as lattice construction
OpenStreetMap tags the tower type as observation
Forest Lookouts lists a Noxubee entry under Noxubee County
Aermotor lookout models came in several standardized heights
evidence.quote: models, which came in a variety of different standardized

evidence.supports: Aermotor made the MC-39 among its lookout models
evidence.quote: the lookout towers, including the LS-50, LS-40 and MC-39

corrections.proposed: Privately owned; site was a county work center of the Mississippi Forestry Commission
corrections.why: The agency field should name who runs or cooperates on the site, not its ownership status. The register lists the site as a former MFC county work center and now privately owned.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 249 ft (76 m). OpenStreetMap's ele tag gives 74 m. The gap is small and unexplained; the story uses the register's figure and says the sources differ.

sources.title: The Aermotor Company: From Windmills to Forest Lookout Towers

notes_for_editor: The register entry is short and undated, and it is the only detailed source; the story says so. Its agency line reads 'Privately Owned' while the description says the site was an MFC county work center, which is why a correction is proposed. The 100 ft height is converted to 30.5 m. Staffing and fire history were not found after two searches and about four page reads. The MC-39 description rests on the register plus one general article on Aermotor models, not on documents about this tower.
